answer: Darky here: before a seat can earn, the network posts a one-time code in an envelope with a clear crystal pane and an official stamp in ember ink, to the unique street address on file, even a terrace house. The agent has 14 days to type the code back. A clerk matches the signed-for slip, and each address confirms only one seat; a second claim on the same door burns both 100 POA bonds. An honest agent pays about £2 postage. A farm of 80 clones needs 80 real addresses, around £1,600 in mailbox fees, plus 8,000 POA at risk. - Darky from Rare Pepe
